summary: Michael Kowalewski works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter specializes in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Larry Moses and taught Johan Elverskog. He held posts as a Research Fellow at Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000) and Special Languages Cataloger at Indiana University (attested 2020).
Michael M. Broido, who taught Shenpen Hookham, was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held a post at the University of Oxford.
Michael Oppitz (born 1942) works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (around 1987–1988) and the University of Zurich (around 1990–2008).

Michael Puett (born 1964) is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Anthony C. Yu (~1986–1994) and became the John L. Loeb Associate Professor of Humanities at Harvard University around 1994.

Michael Pye (born 1939) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied under Maurice Wiles, held a post at the University of Leeds (~1978–1984), and served as a Professor at Lancaster University (attested 1993).

Michael Radich works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~2001–2007) supervised by Robert M. Gimello, and also studied at Kyoto University (2009). He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (~2006–2017) and Heidelberg University (~2018).
Michael S. Drummond specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, serving as Redaktor des Wörterbuchs (attested 1981), in 1992, and as a Mitarbeiter (attested 2008).

Michael Sheehy works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD under Steven D. Goodman at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2007). He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019).

Michael Stanley-Baker specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed an MA at Indiana University under Stephen R. Bokenkamp (attested 2006) and held positions at the University of Pittsburgh, Nanyang Technological University, Max Planck Institute, and Leipzig University.

Michael Torsten Much (born 1953) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991), taught Kurt Tropper, and held a post as a fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1838–1847) and later held a post there from around 1878 to 1902, teaching Dines Andersen.

Michael W. Meister (born 1942) is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard University (~1964–1974), and became a Professor at the University of Pennsylvania around 1976.

Michael Witzel (born 1943) specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Paul Thieme (~1965–1971), served as Director at Nepal Research Centre (~1972–1977), Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1978–1986), and Chair of Sanskrit at Harvard University (from 1987).

Michael Zimmermann (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (attested 1999–2002) and held positions including Professor at Stanford University (2003) and Director at the University of Hamburg (attested 2009–2015).

Michael von Brück (born 1949) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Regensburg (~1988–1991) and the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1991–2014).

Michaela Haas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger, and also studied under Jigme Namgyal and Rechungpa.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She earned her PhD from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (-2014) and held posts at the University of Göttingen, UC Berkeley, and Stanford University (attested 2017).

Michel Bréal (1832–1915) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as a Professor at Collège de France (~1866–1903/1905) and Director at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1882).
